item.research_question: How do axial magnetic fields affect the morphology, total volume, and transverse section area of the primary Al2Cu phase during the directional solidification of hypereutectic Al-Cu alloys, and what is the underlying mechanism involving thermoelectric magnetic forces?
item.processing_route: Directional solidification using a Bridgman type furnace with an upward thermal gradient of 6000 K/m and a constant pulling speed of 2 μm/s, under axial magnetic fields of 0T, 6T, 10T, and 12T provided by a superconductor magnet.
item.test_conditions: Axial magnetic fields ranging from 0 to 14T; solidification in a corundum crucible (3 mm inner diameter) sealed in an argon atmosphere; 3D quantification via synchrotron X-ray tomography (53 KeV beam, 1.3 × 1.3 μm2 pixel size); dislocation analysis via transmission electron microscope.
key_findings: The total volume of the primary Al2Cu phase increases with rising magnetic field intensity.
The transverse section area of each Al2Cu column gradually decreases as the magnetic field increases, indicating refinement.
At 12T, the non-faceted feature of the Al2Cu phase becomes dominating, whereas 90° angles (faceted) are typical without a field.
A torque forms on the Al2Cu column due to thermoelectric magnetic forces (TEMF), causing fragmentation of the continuously grown column.
Strong stresses up to 3.3 × 10^8 N/m^2 are generated in the Al2Cu column by TEMF.
Samples solidified under a 10T magnetic field show a number of dislocations, while those without the field are nearly dislocation-free.
The degree of refinement and growth enhancement increases linearly with the applied magnetic field flux intensity.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute refinement to the fragmentation of the Al2Cu column caused by a torque generated by thermoelectric magnetic forces (TEMF) acting on the solid. Growth enhancement is attributed to TEMF-induced dislocation multiplication, which provides more vacancies for atom attachment, thereby facilitating the growth of the faceted phase. The linear increase in effects is explained by the linear proportionality of TEMF to the magnetic field flux intensity.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The text does not explicitly state future work proposed by the authors.
quotes: With rising magnetic fields, both increase of Al2Cu phase's total volume and decrease of each column's transverse section area were found.
The thermoelectric magnetic forces (TEMF) causing torque and dislocation multiplication in the faceted primary phases were thought dedicate to respectively the refinement and growth enhancement.
It manifests that a number of dislocations form in the sample solidified under magnetic field and nearly dislocation free structure is obtained without the magnetic field.
